blocking.section: Note opening, §§2–3 and §5; dialect §5.1 and accepted 5u3 interpretation

steps.claim: K=4096 bounds INT atoms only. The accepted interpretation imposes no additional cardinality bound on pointer-offset sets or memory intervals and requires preservation of reference sets.
The measured implementation closes pointer sets beyond 4096 even when early-chain-close is false, adds EXT and sets top. The note nevertheless labels this mode the reference.

Construct a CC function containing qalloc/qfree, an internal global X of type [8193 x i8], and 4097 GEP values at offsets 2j for j=0..4096. Combine them with a balanced tree of pointer selects using an i1 parameter. Every offset is in bounds. PT2/PT3 require exactly (0 mod 2)[0,8193), with no EXT and top=false.
steps.by: clause:PT2; clause:PT3; witness:generated LLVM input executed through /usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/opt with .tmp/rung4/prof/p18-D3.so

steps.claim: With -passes=bennett -bennett-dialect=0.2.10 -bennett-analysis-only -bennett-report=/dev/stdout -disable-output and no closing flag, the retained D3 binary returned PTR(@x,0,2), PTR(EXT,0,-1), top=true. Thus the measured default is not the reference analysis. The costs are real, but their attribution entirely to the specified reference is unsupported.

blocking.section: Note §6 Option B; dialect PT6–PT8 and §§6.2–6.4

steps.claim: The reference retains storage intervals and representation widths. A disjoint integer field must not acquire handle provenance; only an actual handle-derived or partially overlapping handle access triggers BD-E-HANDLE-USE.
steps.by: clause:PT6–PT8; clause:§5.2 handle-array propagation requirement; clause:§6.2; clause:§6.4; clause:North Star §3.1

steps.claim: B collapses an object after more than max(64,extent/4) store-created slots and makes subsequent accesses use (X,*), retaining ROOT provenance.

On e-p:64:64, allocate X={ptr,[65 x i8]} and a clean one-wire handle h. Emit 65 separate stores of i8 1 at offsets 8+j, j=0..64; then store h at offset 0. Load i8 at offset 8, zero-extend it to i32, free h and return the integer. X has extent 80, so the threshold is 64. Its handle occupies [0,8); the loaded byte occupies [8,9), with no overlap.

Without early closing, the retained F2 binary accepts and reports AV(v)={INT(0),INT(1)}, top=false, with no ROOT. With -bennett-analysis-early-chain-close it exits 1: “BD-E-HANDLE-USE: §6.2 partial handle read” at the byte load.

This is an additional rejection of a supported, defined program, not merely an expensive executable dispatch domain. It is narrowing even though the widening is conservative for alias analysis and is disclosed.
steps.by: step:<2>1; step:<2>2; step:<2>3; step:<2>4; clause:binding no-narrowing rule

blocking.fix: I would accept Option A. Replace note §6's recommendation with this exact text, retaining the equivalent accepted wording in dialect §5.1: “Retain the §5 reference analysis and the accepted 5u3 interpretation. K=4096 applies only to INT atoms; there is no additional cardinality cutoff for pointer-offset sets or memory intervals. Implementations MAY use exact symbolic sets, factored relations and SCC acceleration instead of enumeration, provided they preserve the reference least fixpoint, storage intervals, representation widths, explicit ROOT and FN alternatives, verdicts, candidate sets and dispatch domains. An implementation time or memory cap reports an unfinished build with the exhausted resource and leaves the implementation obligation open; it does not authorize source rejection or a runtime fault. Unmodified SQLite remains required. All non-exact closing, including the current 4096-pointer-offset rule, remains a non-reference experiment.” For the witness, require accept, AV(v)={INT(0),INT(1)}, no ROOT, and concrete return 1. The other viable route is a redesigned B with this additional rule: “Summary-created overlap MUST NOT establish handle use or escape; retain the original interval-sensitive reference result for those checks. Loss of finite non-handle information MUST have an accepted executable lowering; where that lowering is unavailable, retain the original reference domains rather than reject, block or fault because of widening.” That route needs a separately specified semantic revision and cannot be obtained merely by loosening the constants. I choose A.

For any future B proposal, add in §6: “Thresholds and summaries are defined over represented logical sets, independently of storage representation and worklist scheduling; all affected constraints are reconsidered until that specified result is reached.” Include both store orders of the B2 witness: the retained F2 binary accepts the handle-first order but rejects the handle-last order, so its measurements do not validate an order-independent closing contract.
path_to_accept: 1. Correct the reference labels and attribution as specified in B1; retain the verified measurements as implementation evidence. 2. Replace B with the exact Option A text in B2 and record its representation-only publication route. Keep the existing 5u3 clarification on both tracks. These changes remove the blockers without requiring a completed SQLite performance run; exact-engine implementation and rung-4 production acceptance remain bp-fj1 work.
summary: Revise Option B. I would accept Option A with the quoted replacement text: the measured default already widens beyond the reference, and B demonstrably rejects a valid disjoint-field program. The performance evidence is useful, but does not justify narrowing. No core-scoped blocker.
